quote: Good things, when short, are twice as good.
source: Baltasar Gracián, The Art of Worldly Wisdom, maxim cv, Don’t be a Bore, p. 60 (trans. Joseph Jacobs, Macmillan, 1892)

evidence.where: the Google scan of the Macmillan edition on the Internet Archive; the sentence stands in the middle of maxim cv on p. 60, the table of contents lists cv Don't be a Bore (No cansar) at p. 60, and the dedication to Mrs G. H. Lewis is dated Kilburn, 26th October 1892
evidence.edition: The Art of Worldly Wisdom, trans. Joseph Jacobs, Macmillan and Co., London and New York, 1892
evidence.locator: maxim cv, Don't be a Bore, p. 60

reason: Read verbatim on the page: Brevity flatters and does better business; it gains by courtesy what it loses by curtness. Good things, when short, are twice as good. The proposal gave the maxim's span, pp. 60 to 61; the sentence itself is on p. 60 and the citation now says so.
